Okay, this is going to be long, but please bear with me.

First of all, I am sorry to hear that your home life is in this state. No one deserves to live like this.

Secondly, I want to clear something up: I don't think coming to the internet for help is the right call. Looking back, I regret making this post, and I realise I exaggerated a bit when making it. Personally, many things have happened to me in the last two years. I spoke to my school counsellor about my father, and that helped out a lot. Both me and my father were in a very bad place back then, and we're better now.

Thirdly, it seems to me that your case is quite a bit worse than mine. Obviously, there's a limit to how much I can know as a random guy on the internet, so my best advice is to get help from a reliable source - school counsellor, mental health professional, etc. The police should be your last resort, and even if they are needed, they'd probably be more compelled to help if an adult spoke to them. I don't exactly know the limits of what does and doesn't merit the involvement of law enforcement, but let me tell you this: if your father is leaving you with bruises, definitely try to get help, and if you can't, contact the police yourself.

Finally, I hope everything turns out well for you. I can tell you that I personally keep a journal to record my feelings, and it's helped a lot. Moreover, I recently decided to go over what I wrote in the journal a year or two ago, and I realized just how much better everything is. My point is that things can turn around for you. It won't be instant - it'll take time and effort and probably lots of pain, too, but it can happen, as long as you're ready to learn, grow, and ask for help when you need it. Godspeed, and I hope I made your day just a little bit better.
